propositions: An O_EXCL enrich-drain lock created without owner stamp can leak permanently when the drainer dies between acquire and release, with no staleness check or reclaim path to recover it.

A dead holder's 0-byte lock causes FileExistsError on every subsequent drain attempt, triggering an INFO skip log and returning {"skipped": "lock-held"}, making the enrichment wedge invisible without diagnostic tooling.
Stamped locks must be written after O_EXCL create succeeds (best-effort like mkdir lock) to encode host/ns/pid/start metadata for later staleness adjudication.

Reclamation logic must extract a shared _stamp_is_stale core from lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale and add stamped_file_is_stale(path) to read drain lock stamps and route unrecognised (empty) stamps to the 1h wall-clock ceiling rather than legacy checking.

On FileExistsError, stamped_file_is_stale must be consulted; if stale, the lock is logged at WARNING with holder name and age, unlinked, and create retried exactly once; a second collision skips as today.

Skip logs must move from INFO to WARNING and name the decoded holder so a wedged drain is attributable without running doctor; doctor's drain leg must decode the stamp and report real staleness verdicts instead of not-assessable.
